text: R package vegetation data processing, characterization, classification, applications grassland pasture ecology, phytopastoral analysis, phytosociology. iPastoralist provides tools managing analysing botanical composition data collected using point-quadrat (point-intercept) phytosociological survey methods. package supports conversion standardization vegetation data, calculation biodiversity, pastoral, ecological indicators, numerical classification floristic characterization plant communities. Website: https://marcopittarello.github.io/iPastoralist/

main functionalities iPastoralist organized three complementary analytical components: Vegetation data preparation conversion: processing botanical survey data converting species frequency cover measurements suitable quantitative formats. Vegetation characterization: calculating biodiversity indices, Pastoral Value, ecological indicator values, descriptors floristic composition. Vegetation classification interpretation: supporting numerical vegetation classification, identification diagnostic characteristic species, interpretation vegetation groups according phytopastoral phytosociological approaches. components can used independently combined integrated workflow vegetation analysis.

iPastoralist designed work botanical composition data collected using two main survey methods: Point-quadrat / pinpoint (point-intercept) method: plant species recorded fixed intervals along linear transect (Daget Poissonet, 1971). Phytosociological method: plant species occurring within vegetation plots recorded, cover visually estimated. point-quadrat surveys, package also supports datasets including occasional species, .e., species recorded within surrounding vegetation plot intercepted along transect. particularly relevant point-intercept sampling may fail detect rare low-abundance species, can nevertheless contribute biodiversity vegetation characterization. package particularly suited grassland pasture studies, although several functions can also applied vegetation types.
